title: A bell on my ankle stops my sleepwalking. Tonight it rang outside my bedroom door.
story:
The bell rang in the hallway just after three. Sour and flat, the way it always sounds.

I was lying in bed. Awake. And that bell is tied to my ankle.

I started sleepwalking last month. I'd wake up in the yard, in the kitchen, once in the car with the engine running. So I bought a little brass bell at a yard sale, cracked down one side, and tied it on every night with a shoelace. If I got up, that sour ring would wake me.

Now it was ringing outside my door. Step. Ring. Step. Ring. Slow, like someone trying very hard to be quiet.

"Hello?" I said.

The ringing stopped. Then my own voice answered, sleepy and calm. "Go back to bed. I've got it tonight."

I crossed the room in two steps and locked the door. The handle turned once from the other side. Then footsteps went down the stairs, and the front door opened and closed.

I sat on the floor, shaking, and the bell on my ankle chimed. Bright. Clean. Perfect.

I pulled my foot into the moonlight. The brass was smooth. No crack.

So whose ankle is this?
premise: sleepwalker's cracked yard-sale bell rings in the hallway while he's awake in bed; his own voice tells him to go back to sleep and leaves the house; the bell on his own ankle has no crack, so he is the copy
